records.name: St Magnus Cathedral
records.description: St Magnus Cathedral is a Church of Scotland parish church in Kirkwall, the main town of Orkney, a group of islands off the north coast of mainland Scotland. Originally a Roman Catholic cathedral, it is the oldest cathedral in Scotland and the most northerly cathedral in the United Kingdom.

records.name: Bishop's Palace
records.description: The Bishop's Palace, Kirkwall is a 12th-century palace built at the same time as the adjacent St Magnus Cathedral in the centre of Kirkwall, Orkney, Scotland. It housed the cathedral's first bishop, William the Old of the Norwegian Catholic Church who took his authority from the Archbishop of Nidaros (Trondheim).

records.name: Earl's Palace
records.description: The Earl's Palace is a ruined Renaissance-style palace near St Magnus's Cathedral in the centre of Kirkwall, Orkney, Scotland. Built by Patrick, Earl of Orkney, its construction began in 1607 and was largely undertaken via forced labour. Today, the ruins are open to the public.

records.name: Orkney Museum
records.description: The Orkney Museum, formerly Tankerness House Museum, is a history museum in Kirkwall, Orkney, Scotland. Run by Orkney Islands Council, the museum covers the history of the Orkney Islands from the Stone Age through the Picts and Vikings to the present day.

records.name: Highland Park Distillery
records.description: Highland Park distillery is an Island single malt Scotch whisky distillery located in Kirkwall on the Orkney Islands, Scotland. It is the northernmost single malt Scotch whisky distillery.

records.name: Scapa Distillery
records.description: Scapa distillery is a Scotch whisky distillery on The Mainland of Orkney, Scotland on the shore of Scapa Flow near the town of Kirkwall. Scapa is the third-northernmost whisky distillery in Scotland, 1⁄2 mile south of the Highland Park Distillery.

records.name: The Peedie Sea
records.description: The Peedie Sea is a urban nature reserve stop in or near Kirkwall, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Orkney Wireless Museum
records.description: The Orkney Wireless Museum in Kirkwall, Orkney, Scotland, houses a collection of domestic and military wireless equipment. It developed from the private collection of the late Jim MacDonald from St Margaret's Hope and marks the importance of wireless communications in Orkney during World War II.

records.name: Tankerness House Gardens
records.description: Formal gardens beside the Orkney Museum offering a quiet pause in the middle of Kirkwall's historic core.

records.name: Kirkwall Harbour
records.description: Busy harbour that remains one of Orkney's main transport gateways for ferries, yachts and cruise ships.

records.name: St Olaf's Kirk
records.description: St Olaf's Kirk is a historic church stop in or near Kirkwall, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Scapa Beach
records.description: Sheltered sandy bay south of Kirkwall, popular for a coastal walk close to town.

records.name: Italian Chapel
records.description: The Italian Chapel is a highly ornate Catholic chapel on Lamb Holm in Orkney, Scotland. It was built during the Second World War by Italian prisoners of war, who were housed on the previously uninhabited island while they constructed the Churchill Barriers to the east of Scapa Flow.

records.name: Churchill Barriers
records.description: The Churchill Barriers are four causeways in the Orkney islands with a total length of 2.3 kilometres (1.4 mi). They link the Orkney Mainland in the north to the island of South Ronaldsay via Burray and the two smaller islands of Lamb Holm and Glimps Holm.

records.name: Ring of Brodgar
records.description: The Ring of Brodgar is a Neolithic henge and stone circle about 6 miles north-east of Stromness on Mainland, the largest island in Orkney, Scotland. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site known as the Heart of Neolithic Orkney.

records.name: Stones of Stenness
records.description: Stones of Stenness is a prehistoric site stop in or near Stenness, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Maeshowe
records.description: Maeshowe is a Neolithic chambered cairn and passage grave situated on Mainland Orkney, Scotland. It was probably built around 2800 BC. In the archaeology of Scotland, it gives its name to the Maeshowe type of chambered cairn, which is limited to Orkney.

records.name: Broch of Gurness
records.description: The Broch of Gurness is an Iron Age broch village on the northeast coast of Mainland Orkney in Scotland overlooking Eynhallow Sound, about 15 miles north-west of Kirkwall. It once housed a substantial community. It was discovered by the Orkney poet and naturalist Robert Rendall in 1929.

records.name: Brough of Birsay
records.description: Brough of Birsay is a prehistoric site stop in or near Birsay, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Cuween Hill Chambered Cairn
records.description: Cuween Hill Chambered Cairn is a chambered cairn stop in or near Finstown, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Rennibister Earth House
records.description: Rennibister Earth House is a prehistoric site stop in or near Firth, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Wideford Hill Chambered Cairn
records.description: Wideford Hill Chambered Cairn is a chambered cairn stop in or near Kirkwall, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Earl's Bu
records.description: Earl's Bu is a historic site stop in or near Orphir, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Scapa Flow viewpoint
records.description: Scapa Flow viewpoint is a viewpoint stop in or near Mainland, Orkney, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Tomb of the Eagles
records.description: Tomb of the Eagles is a archaeological site stop in or near South Ronaldsay, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Orphir Round Church
records.description: Orphir Round Church is a historic church stop in or near Orphir, suitable for visitors exploring Kirkwall and the surrounding area.

records.name: Deerness Distillery viewpoint
records.description: Eastern cliffs and sea views make Deerness a memorable scenic detour from Kirkwall.

records.name: Kirkwall Town Centre
records.description: Compact Norse-rooted centre of narrow lanes, sandstone buildings and independent shops around the cathedral.

records.name: Skara Brae
records.description: UNESCO-listed 5,000-year-old Neolithic village and the best-preserved prehistoric settlement in northern Europe.

records.name: Pier Arts Centre
records.description: Major modern art gallery in Stromness noted for works connected to Barbara Hepworth and the St Ives school.

records.name: Scapa Flow
records.description: Vast natural anchorage central to twentieth-century naval history, including the scuttling of the German High Seas Fleet and world-famous wreck diving.

records.name: Skaill House
records.description: Historic laird's house beside Skara Brae, closely linked to the site's nineteenth-century rediscovery.

records.name: Bay of Skaill
records.description: Sweeping west Mainland bay beside Skara Brae, with a sandy beach and wide Atlantic views.

records.name: Old Man of Hoy
records.description: Iconic sandstone sea stack rising from Hoy's cliffs, one of the best-known natural landmarks in Britain.

records.name: Orkney Fossil and Heritage Centre
records.description: Local heritage centre with island history exhibits and fossil displays gathered from Orkney's geology-rich shores.

records.name: Kirbuster Farm Museum
records.description: Preserved traditional farmstead presenting rural Orkney life in an eighteenth- and nineteenth-century setting.

records.name: Minehowe
records.description: Remarkable Iron Age underground structure reached by a spiral stair, part of an important excavated settlement landscape.

records.name: Brough of Deerness
records.description: Headland walk to a tidal island with Norse and medieval remains perched dramatically above the sea.

records.name: Mull Head Nature Reserve
records.description: Clifftop reserve and walking area on Orkney's east coast with sea arches, seabirds and views over the North Sea.

records.name: Dwarfie Stane
records.description: Unique rock-cut Neolithic tomb on Hoy, carved directly into a massive block of sandstone.
